brief: Goldman's Vol Panic Index closed Friday at 9.8/10 with SPX below 7,000. Historically such panic signals a buying opportunity, but two complications apply: the Fed is hiking, not cutting (in five prior panic-above-9 episodes during hiking regimes, three-month forward returns averaged only +0.4%), and positioning is mixed. Hedge funds have deleveraged sharply (net leverage at the 1st percentile, beta-adjusted leverage at a five-year low, heavy shorting, momentum exposure flipped negative, the HF VIP basket underperforming by 14pp), and the HF community itself expects more selling, while mutual funds, ETFs and asset managers remain relatively well invested and expect HFs to be forced to buy back higher. So panic and HF capitulation are extreme, but the broad investor washout that typically drives the strongest rebounds has not happened. Goldman draws a partial Q4 2018 analog, when panic preceded another leg lower, but notes today's Cyclicals (+12% YTD) are far more resilient than in 2018 (-23%), reflecting AI-to-ex-AI rotation rather than outright equity downside. Research frames SPX scenarios from 5,800 (valuation normalization) to 8,100 (earnings confidence restored), and the desk's inclination is that equities are near a tactical entry, preferring to sell puts over chasing stocks given still-elevated broader positioning and an unresolved AI earnings debate.
